attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following cusp fluctuation law: for Aztec diamonds of order N with fixed generic positive 3x3-periodic edge weights possessing an explicit cusp singularity of the frozen-rough arctic curve predicted by the spectral/amobeal discriminant equation, the height function and associated particle system in the cusp scaling window of tangential width of order N^{3/4} and normal width of order N^{1/2} about the cusp tip, with explicit polynomial centering from the degenerate double-critical action function of the Kasteleyn inverse, converge to the Pearcey process with its standard gap probabilities; parameter scope is all fixed generic positive 3x3-periodic weights and every generic arctic cusp of that type; a complete answer is a rigorous proof of the stated Pearcey limit with the stated exponents and explicit centering, or a rigorous disproof by establishing a different cusp exponent, different limiting process, or absence of such a limit.
decisive_failure: Single-lane one-hour session without access to bespoke matrix steepest-descent contour machinery; scalar-model numerics support exponents only at heuristic level; no uniform spectral discriminant or gap-probability analysis was completed, so no claim about the truth or falsity of the Pearcey cusp law is made.
